title: US vows to squeeze Iran’s economy to its limits | The National
gist: The Trump administration is pivoting to economic strangulation of Iran -- new Treasury measures, Section 311 and the Lindsey Graham Act -- but analysts including Rachel Ziemba and Ryan Bohl say the naval blockade, which has already cut Iranian oil exports over 80% and costs Tehran $435 million a day, has done far more than incremental sanctions, while further escalation risks friction with China ahead of the Trump-Xi summit.

themes.theme: US pivots to economic strangulation of Iran

insights.claim: The Trump administration is signalling it is ready to push Iran's economy to its limits after already imposing financial pressure and a naval blockade meant to force Tehran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.
insights.speaker: Kyle Fitzgerald
insights.so_what: Marks an explicit US shift toward economic escalation over military escalation in the six-month Iran conflict -- watch for new sanctions packages rather than new strikes.
insights.locator: President Donald Trump's administration is signalling

insights.claim: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the US is preparing to announce new measures amounting to a "combination of economic isolation like the world has never seen before."
insights.speaker: Kyle Fitzgerald
insights.so_what: Signals a major new sanctions package is imminent -- a catalyst to watch for Iran-linked shipping, crypto and banking names.
insights.quote: combination of economic isolation like the world has never seen before
insights.locator: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told Newsmax

insights.claim: US Energy Secretary Chris Wright said Iran has "one card" left in the Strait of Hormuz "and it's shrinking in size," while the US ability to escort products through the waterway is growing.
insights.speaker: Kyle Fitzgerald
insights.so_what: Suggests the US views the blockade/escort strategy as increasingly decisive, which should continue pressuring Iran-linked oil flows and freight insurance costs.
insights.locator: Mr Wright told Fox News that Iran had

insights.claim: The renewed US emphasis on economic pain marks a shift toward squeezing Tehran financially rather than immediately escalating Washington's military campaign, after nearly six months of war.
insights.speaker: Kyle Fitzgerald
insights.so_what: A de-escalation-via-sanctions posture reduces near-term kinetic risk but extends the sanctions overhang on Iran-exposed trade and shipping.
insights.locator: The renewed emphasis on economic pain marks

themes.theme: Iran's economy is already deteriorating sharply

insights.claim: Iran is the second-most sanctioned country in the world, with more than 6,000 sanctions issued against its financial, energy and petrochemical, aviation and cryptocurrency sectors, on top of a secondary-sanctions framework targeting third-country trade with Tehran.
insights.speaker: Kyle Fitzgerald
insights.so_what: Establishes the scale of existing sanctions coverage -- any new package is layering onto an already near-maximal sanctions regime.
insights.locator: Iran remains the second-most sanctioned country

insights.claim: Iranian inflation accelerated to a 53.9% pace between April 20 and May 20, 2026, up from 36.8% over the same period a year earlier, according to the central bank.
insights.speaker: Kyle Fitzgerald
insights.so_what: Sharply accelerating inflation is a hard data point confirming the sanctions/blockade squeeze is biting domestically.
insights.locator: Figures from the central bank showed inflation

insights.claim: The IMF expects Iran's economy to contract 6% this year, and the rial has recently sunk to an all-time low against the dollar.
insights.speaker: Kyle Fitzgerald
insights.so_what: A 6% GDP contraction plus currency collapse points to a deepening economic crisis that raises regime stability risk.
insights.locator: The International Monetary Fund expects a contraction

insights.claim: Iran's Foreign Ministry says the country will not be broken by renewed sanctions pressure, arguing it has withstood such measures for decades.
insights.speaker: Kyle Fitzgerald
insights.so_what: Tehran's public defiance signals it may be willing to absorb further economic pain rather than capitulate quickly, arguing against a fast resolution.
insights.quote: Iran has demonstrated over decades that it will not be strangled by these exhausted refrains
insights.locator: Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmail Baghaei

themes.theme: Washington's remaining economic levers are limited

insights.claim: Ryan Bohl, senior MENA analyst at the Rane Network, says the viable economic levers the US has left against Iran are limited: "there's not a lot."
insights.speaker: Kyle Fitzgerald
insights.so_what: A sober read from a regional analyst tempers expectations that new sanctions alone can force an Iranian capitulation.
insights.quote: The economic levers that it [the US] has got left that are viable – there's not a lot
insights.locator: Ryan Bohl, a senior Middle East

insights.claim: Iran relies on a shadow banking system of Iran-based exchange houses and foreign companies to sell oil and other goods abroad, launder proceeds, and fund its proxy groups, military and weapons programmes; the US Treasury targeted this network -- including crypto exchanges and currency networks -- for the eighth time this year last week.
insights.speaker: Kyle Fitzgerald
insights.so_what: The shadow banking/crypto network is the operational chokepoint for Iran's sanctions evasion -- expect continued Treasury actions against exchange houses and crypto rails.
insights.locator: This network consists of Iran-based exchange houses

insights.claim: Rachel Ziemba, founder of Ziemba Insights, expects more US Treasury designations targeting Iran's alternate channels, but questions whether new designations will meaningfully affect Iran's economy given the regime's ability to circumvent sanctions -- saying they will likely be about "closing loopholes rather than additional components."
insights.speaker: Kyle Fitzgerald
insights.so_what: A contrarian check on the sanctions-escalation narrative: incremental designations may have diminishing marginal effect on Iran's economy.
insights.quote: They'll probably be more about closing loopholes rather than additional components
insights.locator: Considering the regime's ability to circumvent

insights.claim: The US could invoke Section 311 of the Patriot Act, which lets the Treasury secretary designate foreign financial jurisdictions over money-laundering concerns, as an additional lever against Iran.
insights.speaker: Kyle Fitzgerald
insights.so_what: A specific legal tool to watch for escalation -- Section 311 designations could hit third-country banks handling Iran-linked flows.
insights.locator: There are additional measures the US can use

insights.claim: The newly passed Lindsey Graham Act would let Trump impose secondary sanctions and tariffs on countries that keep buying oil from Iran and Russia, but Bohl warns it would likely push energy prices up, which Trump doesn't want.
insights.speaker: Kyle Fitzgerald
insights.so_what: Creates a policy tension: the most aggressive available lever risks the one outcome (higher oil/gas prices) the administration is trying to avoid politically.
insights.quote: The issue is it would probably cause energy prices to go up, which Trump doesn't want to see
insights.locator: The Lindsey Graham Act, passed by the Senate

themes.theme: The naval blockade has been the real game-changer

insights.claim: Iran's seaborne crude exports fell from 2.7 million barrels per day in February to 502,000 bpd in May after the US imposed a maritime blockade on Iranian ports, per data from energy intelligence firm Kpler.
insights.speaker: Kyle Fitzgerald
insights.so_what: An over 80% collapse in seaborne exports quantifies the blockade's bite -- a template for how physical enforcement outperforms financial sanctions alone.
insights.locator: Its seaborne crude exports fell from 2.7 million bpd

insights.claim: Iranian crude exports averaged 1.18 million bpd in July 2026, well below the roughly 2.5 million bpd peak reached in 2017 under the Iran nuclear deal.
insights.speaker: Kyle Fitzgerald
insights.so_what: Benchmarks current Iranian export levels against the JCPOA-era peak, showing the blockade has pushed exports to a fraction of prior capacity.
insights.locator: Iranian crude exports averaged 1.18 million bpd

insights.claim: The US Treasury said average loadings of Iranian oil declined from 1.8 million bpd before the war to less than 500,000 bpd over the past month.
insights.speaker: Kyle Fitzgerald
insights.so_what: Confirms via an independent official source the scale of the export collapse -- a leading indicator for Iran's hard-currency revenue.
insights.locator: The Treasury Department said average loadings

insights.claim: The naval blockade has cost Iran an estimated $435 million in economic activity every day, according to research from the Foundation for Defence of Democracies.
insights.speaker: Kyle Fitzgerald
insights.so_what: Quantifies the daily fiscal bleed from the blockade -- a concrete number for modelling Iran's reserve depletion timeline.
insights.locator: The blockade has cost Iran $435 million

insights.claim: Ziemba calls the blockade "a game-changer in terms of further economic effect," more consequential than incremental sanctions designations.
insights.speaker: Kyle Fitzgerald
insights.so_what: Physical interdiction, not new designations, is the dominant lever -- investors should weight naval/blockade headlines over sanctions-list updates.
insights.quote: That’s been a game-changer in terms of further economic effect
insights.locator: “That’s been a game-changer

insights.claim: The blockade cut off a key Iranian oil buyer in China, which normally takes in about 90% of Iran's oil exports and is one of the few countries willing to absorb sanctions risk by using so-called teapot refineries.
insights.speaker: Kyle Fitzgerald
insights.so_what: China is the single largest marginal buyer of Iranian crude -- any China-specific secondary sanctions would be the highest-impact but also highest-friction lever available.
insights.locator: It also cut off a key purchaser in China

insights.claim: TankerTrackers estimated Iran exported more than 50 million barrels of crude during the brief window when the blockade was lifted, with much of it moving off-transponder to India and China, which took the opportunity to buy cheap oil to clear backlogs.
insights.speaker: Kyle Fitzgerald
insights.so_what: Shows how quickly Iranian export volumes rebound the moment blockade enforcement eases -- underscores that sustained pressure, not one-off actions, is what constrains Tehran.
insights.quote: Because so much of it was off transponders, it's hard to tell where all of it went, but it flooded out to India, to China, to countries that basically had a backlog and were taking that opportunity to get as cheap oil as they could
insights.locator: TankerTrackers said it estimated Iran exported

themes.theme: Escalation risks friction with China ahead of the Trump-Xi summit

insights.claim: Further secondary sanctions and economic measures against Iran risk alienating key US partners while inflaming tensions with China, described as the US's chief economic rival.
insights.speaker: Kyle Fitzgerald
insights.so_what: Iran sanctions policy is now entangled with US-China relations -- a variable that could complicate or be complicated by trade negotiations.
insights.locator: Secondary sanctions and further measures could also

insights.claim: Alex Zerden, a former Treasury official and founder of Capitol Peak Strategies, says Iran sanctions policy is "absolutely intertwined with the broader bilateral relationship between the US and China."
insights.speaker: Kyle Fitzgerald
insights.so_what: Frames Iran sanctions as a proxy battleground within the broader US-China relationship, relevant to positioning around the upcoming summit.
insights.quote: It's absolutely intertwined with the broader bilateral relationship between the US and China
insights.locator: Alex Zerden, a former Treasury official

insights.claim: Trump warned Russia and China that supporting Iran "would be very bad for them," while separately acknowledging that any support the two countries provided to Iran had only a minimal impact.
insights.speaker: Kyle Fitzgerald
insights.so_what: Trump's mixed messaging suggests he is calibrating pressure on China carefully rather than committing to full-scale secondary sanctions against Beijing.
insights.quote: would be very bad for them
insights.locator: He warned Russia and China last month

insights.claim: Trump is due to host Chinese President Xi Jinping next month for a high-stakes summit, with tensions already simmering over trade and Beijing's ties to Tehran, creating an opportunity to extend last year's trade truce even as Iran pressure risks adding new friction.
insights.speaker: Kyle Fitzgerald
insights.so_what: The Trump-Xi summit is a near-term catalyst where Iran sanctions policy and the US-China trade truce could collide -- a key date to watch for market-moving headlines.
insights.locator: The US President is due to host Chinese President

insights.claim: Zerden says the key open question is how provocative or escalatory the US will be toward China in the lead-up to the Trump-Xi summit or subsequent summits.
insights.speaker: Kyle Fitzgerald
insights.so_what: Frames US restraint or escalation toward China over Iran as the swing factor to watch heading into the summit.
insights.quote: The question is to the degree and how provocative or escalatory the US might be in the lead-up to the next summit or subsequent summits
insights.locator: Mr Zerden said
